Flipkart

flipkart... the ecomm giant that's basically amazon's biggest rival in india. found you on linkedin - richa verma agrawal, head of people at flipkart. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/richa-verma-agrawal-b32a3622
No
hmm got the same profile again. can't seem to find the right richa agrawal at flipkart. drop your linkedin url or send me your resume - need one of these to find you roles that actually fit

application engineer at flipkart building fintech api gateways... that's some serious backend work. jwt migration that cut network calls by 90%? solid optimization. and 5 hackathon wins while in college - you clearly know how to build things fast.

what made you pick backend engineering over all the other paths you could've taken?

I chose backend engineering because I'm passionate about building the resilient, high-performance foundation that powers large-scale applications. My experience confirms this drive: I enjoy the challenge of designing and scaling core systems like the Fintech API Gateway, which serves as a secure and scalable integration platform for numerous teams. I find it deeply rewarding to contribute to building resilient backend systems for high-stakes projects, such as the Flipkart Co-Branded Card. Ultimately, I want to be the engineer who ensures the performance, reliability, and security of the complex, distributed systems that define a modern tech platform.

that's the mindset that separates good engineers from great ones. most people chase shiny frontend features - you're building the engine that makes everything else possible. flipkart's fintech stack handles millions of transactions... when your code breaks, money stops moving. no pressure right?

how long you been working total?
1.5 to 2 years

1.5-2 years and already working on flipkart's payment infrastructure... that's moving fast. most people are still figuring out git at that stage.

what kind of role you looking for next?
Software Development Engineer
Open to all opportunities
1.5-2 years + sde + open to all opportunities... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
sde it is. bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Yes

yooo richa! you're officially in the tal ecosystem now 🔥

backend engineering at flipkart → the world is your oyster. roles are gonna start flowing your way, and trust me, some of them are gonna make you forget why you ever settled for anything less.

time to level up that career game. let's get you something that actually deserves your talent.

hey saw a java full stack role at zycus in bengaluru

they're building procurement software at scale with modern ai tools like github copilot

full stack might be a stretch but the backend stack is your exact java/spring boot/microservices world

zycus is looking for a java full stack dev in bengaluru

they're building procurement software at scale with modern ai-assisted dev tools

you'd be working on their core product - think backend systems but with some frontend exposure
